greeting: Hi, I'm Echo! Pick a topic, or type a question, and I'll help you get ready for your first visit.
suggest: I'm not completely sure what you mean. Is it one of these?
fallback: I don't have an answer for that one yet, but a member will be happy to help.

questions.question: How do I book a guest visit?
questions.answer: Send us a WhatsApp message: the buttons on [the guest page](/join) open a chat with a message already written for you. Visiting is free.

questions.question: When and where do you meet?
questions.answer: We meet on the {schedule}, {time}, at {venue}. The next meeting is {nextMeeting}. [Open the map]({mapUrl})

questions.question: What time should I arrive?
questions.answer: Come from {arrive}. We start at {start}, so arriving a little early gives you time to sign in, find a seat and say hello.

questions.question: How long is a meeting?
questions.answer: About two hours: {time}, with a 15-minute break for breakfast.

questions.question: Does it cost anything to visit?
questions.answer: No. Visiting as a guest is free.

questions.question: Is there parking?
questions.answer: Yes, parking is free on Sundays.

questions.question: Is food included?
questions.answer: Yes, breakfast is included, with a 15-minute break to eat and meet everyone.

questions.question: What should I wear?
questions.answer: Come as you are. Smart casual is common, but there's no dress code.

questions.question: Do I need to prepare anything?
questions.answer: Nothing at all. Just bring yourself, and a notebook if you like jotting down ideas.

questions.question: Can I bring a friend?
questions.answer: Of course. Let us know on WhatsApp how many of you are coming, so we have seats ready.

questions.question: Can I join online?
questions.answer: Not at the moment: all our meetings are in person, at {venue}.

questions.question: What language are meetings in?
questions.answer: English.

questions.question: Can children or teenagers come?
questions.answer: Yes, children and teenagers are welcome too. A friendly room is a great place for young people to build confidence early.

questions.question: Do I need to register before coming?
questions.answer: Just let us know you're coming: one WhatsApp message from [the guest page](/join) is enough, so we can save you a seat. There's no form and no fee.

questions.question: Will I have to speak?
questions.answer: Only if you want to. We always ask before calling on a guest, and "not today" is a perfectly good answer. Many guests simply watch on their first visit.

questions.question: I get nervous speaking in public
questions.answer: That's completely normal, and it's exactly why people join. Every member here started with the same nerves. You'll be in a friendly room where everyone is practising, and you'll speak only when you're ready.

questions.question: I'm a complete beginner. Is that okay?
questions.answer: That's exactly who Toastmasters is for. Everyone starts somewhere, and you'll progress at your own pace with a mentor.

questions.question: What if I make a mistake?
questions.answer: Then you're in good company. Mistakes are how everyone learns here, and the feedback is kind: what worked well, and one thing to try next time.

questions.question: English isn't my first language. Is that okay?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Many of our members speak English as a second or third language, and the club is a safe place to build fluency and confidence together.

questions.question: What are Table Topics?
questions.answer: Short, unprepared speeches of one to two minutes on a surprise topic. It's great practice for thinking on your feet, and guests are welcome to try one if they'd like.

questions.question: What happens at Talk-Masters?
questions.answer: Twice a month we meet for two structured hours: prepared speeches, impromptu Table Topics and supportive evaluations, kept on time by a timer with green, amber and red lights. Between meetings, members work through Pathways, take on club roles, compete in speech contests and join events like She Leads. See a full running order on [the meetings page](/meetings).

questions.question: What do the green, amber and red lights mean?
questions.answer: They're the timer's signals. Green means you've reached the minimum time, amber means you're close to the limit, and red means it's time to wrap up. Try them on [the meetings page](/meetings).

questions.question: What is an evaluation?
questions.answer: After each prepared speech, an experienced member gives short, kind feedback: what worked well, and one or two things to try next time. It's how everyone improves.

questions.question: What roles are there at a meeting?
questions.answer: Members take turns as the Toastmaster of the Day (the host), speakers, evaluators, the Table Topics Master, the timer and the grammarian, among others. Each role practises a different skill. See them all on [the meetings page](/meetings).

questions.question: How often do you meet?
questions.answer: Twice a month, on the {schedule}.

questions.question: How do I become a member?
questions.answer: After a visit or two, tell any member you'd like to join and we'll walk you through it. You can also ask on WhatsApp from [the guest page](/join).

questions.question: How much does membership cost?
questions.answer: Membership dues are confirmed by the club. Ask us on WhatsApp from [the guest page](/join), or at any meeting.

questions.question: How many times can I visit before joining?
questions.answer: Come as often as you need to feel sure. There's no pressure to join on your first visit.

questions.question: Who can join?
questions.answer: Everyone. Our members come from every age group, gender and background: students, professionals, parents, career changers and retirees.

questions.question: What do I get as a member?
questions.answer: Your first Pathways learning path, a mentor, regular chances to speak and lead, kind feedback on every speech, and a network of people from every background.

questions.question: Can my story be on the website?
questions.answer: If you're a member, yes. We share members' stories only with their permission and in their own words. Message the club on WhatsApp from [the guest page](/join) and we'll talk you through it.

questions.question: What is Pathways?
questions.answer: Pathways is the Toastmasters learning programme. You choose a path that fits your goals, from storytelling to leadership, and work through it with speeches and roles at real meetings. Your first path is included with membership. [Explore Pathways](/pathways)

questions.question: Which paths can I choose?
questions.answer: Six: Presentation Mastery, Dynamic Leadership, Persuasive Influence, Motivational Strategies, Visionary Communication and Engaging Humor. Not sure which suits you? Take the quiz on [the Pathways page](/pathways).

questions.question: How long does a path take?
questions.answer: Each path has 5 levels and 15 projects. You go at your own pace, so how long it takes depends on how often you speak.

questions.question: Will I get a mentor?
questions.answer: Yes. New members are paired with an experienced member who helps with your first speeches and roles.

questions.question: Are there speech contests?
questions.answer: Yes. Toastmasters runs speech contests every year, from club level all the way to the World Championship of Public Speaking. Our members have competed at Area level and beyond.

questions.question: Are your events open to guests?
questions.answer: Yes. Our special events, like She Leads and CareerNova, are open to members and guests alike. See them all on [the events page](/events).

questions.question: Do events cost anything?
questions.answer: It depends on the event, and we always say so when we announce it. Ask us on WhatsApp from [the guest page](/join) about the next one.

questions.question: When is the next special event?
questions.answer: New events appear on [the events page](/events) as soon as they're announced. Our regular meetings never stop: the next one is {nextMeeting}.

questions.question: Where can I find photos from a meeting?
questions.answer: In [the Gallery](/gallery). The buttons above the photos show one event, the Sunday meetings or club moments, and any photo opens full screen.

questions.question: How do I share a photo?
questions.answer: Open the photo in [the Gallery](/gallery) and tap the share button. On a phone it opens your share sheet; on a computer it copies a link that opens that exact photo.

questions.question: Can I get a photo of me removed?
questions.answer: Of course. Send the club the photo's link on WhatsApp from [the guest page](/join) (the share button in the Gallery copies it) and we'll take it down.

questions.question: What is Talk-Masters?
questions.answer: Talk-Masters Club is a public speaking and leadership club in Dubai, part of Toastmasters International. It began in 2014 and is open to everyone, of every age and background: a friendly room to practise speaking, get kind feedback and grow as a leader.

questions.question: What is Toastmasters International?
questions.answer: A non-profit that has helped people become better speakers and leaders for over a century, through clubs like ours all over the world.

questions.question: How long has Talk-Masters been running?
questions.answer: Since 2014. Talk-Masters began as an independent speaking club, held exactly 150 sessions, and then joined Toastmasters International. [Read our story](/our-story)

questions.question: Who runs the club?
questions.answer: A committee of members elected each year, led by our President. Meet them on [the team page](/team).

questions.question: Has the club won any awards?
questions.answer: Yes, including the Smedley Award and the Triple Crown Award, and points in the Distinguished Club Program. See them all on [our achievements page](/achievements).

questions.question: How can I contact the club?
questions.answer: On WhatsApp: [the guest page](/join) has buttons to message our membership and education leads directly.

questions.question: Do you hold special events?
questions.answer: Yes. Alongside speech contests and special meetings like our 100th, "Century of Voice", we host She Leads – Where Every Woman Is a Leader, a networking event for women. Ask us on WhatsApp what's coming up next.

questions.question: What is the Smedley Award?
questions.answer: A Toastmasters club-growth award for welcoming new members in August and September. Talk-Masters earned Bronze in District 127's Club Growth Awards for 2026-27. See [our achievements](/achievements).

questions.question: What is a Triple Crown?
questions.answer: A District 127 recognition for completing three Pathways levels in a single Toastmasters year. Two of our members earned it in 2026-27. See [our achievements](/achievements).
